correctness.rationale: From the affine axioms, NN^T=qI+J exactly, giving an exhaustive five-eigenvalue Laplacian decomposition with multiplicities 1,1,q,q²−1,q²−1. PBH gives the q²−1 total lower bound; the line-kernel modes force q distinct controlled parallel classes. Restriction on the two large eigenspaces yields exactly the square determinant test for each minimal set, and the radial modes are automatically detected. The concurrent-pencil construction has determinant proportional to 1−q≠0. Its signatures 0,e_i,all-ones form an affine circuit, proving 2q(q−1)^q valid omissions per pencil and 2q³(q+1)(q−1)^q globally. The actual embedded verifier was executed with 3514 finite checks, including exhaustive rational PBH testing at q=2 and modular Kalman checks at q=3 and q=5; no finite test substitutes for the all-q proof. Scope is unit-weight, existing planes and independent coordinate inputs.

originality.rationale: Originality is assigned to the complete minimum-coordinate-placement criterion, compulsory line-direction coverage, simultaneous optimal placement and exact concurrent-pencil census, not to PBH, the affine incidence spectrum, or the general maximum-multiplicity driver count. Full accessible texts of Zhang–Camlibel–Cao (2011) and Yuan et al. (2013) were inspected: the former develops graph-partition/distance-regular leader tests and the latter covers the general multiplicity count and algorithmic row selection, but neither gives a point–line affine-plane placement criterion or a q-dependent geometric census. The affine incidence graph is biregular rather than distance regular. Actual topic and alias searches in primary literature and the mathematical record found no stronger explicit covering formula. Priority risk from unidentified specialist work remains documented.
residual_risks: An indexed or inaccessible specialist publication could contain the same affine incidence placement and pencil enumeration; search absence is not proof of unique priority.
Generic PBH theory implies the rank-test framework, so novelty lies in the closed affine-geometric characterization and exact count rather than in PBH or the maximal-multiplicity principle.
The Yuan et al. supplementary PDF was not materially inspected; the openly accessible main full text was read.

value.rationale: The graph family is a natural biregular incidence network. Restricted leader-type availability has meaningful geometric consequences: every controlling selection needs q line directions, the total and line-controller minima can be achieved simultaneously, an exact incidence determinant classifies all minimal location patterns and an explicit uniform nontrivial count enumerates the natural concurrent-pencil optimal family. This provides a usable design and counting theorem for every existing finite affine plane, including non-Desarguesian examples, exceeding a routine eigenvalue multiplicity computation or an arbitrary finite census.
